Definition: an embrasure or opening with bevelled jam
BiblicalUsage: Narrow lights in the temple were windows cut on a slope, wider within than without, so the light fell deep into the house. Solomon made them for the temple, and the king's house had windows in three rows, and light was against light in three ranks.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe narrow lights were enough for the temple, because a little light set right fills the whole house.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
